afternoon.name: An afternoon
afternoon.line: One sitting, or two. Nothing here needs weeks.
afternoon.after: Done in a day, and it stays done. The room it lives in has more like it.

weeks.name: A few weeks
weeks.line: A little most days, and it is yours before the month is out.
weeks.after: That is the whole ladder. If it caught you, the room it lives in has more.

months.name: A few months
months.line: About three months of a little most days. Every ladder in the school stops around there.
months.after: That is where the ladder stops — about three months in, at something real you can actually do. Nothing in the school runs for years, because a chain you cannot finish stops being a chain. Past here it is yours to carry on, on your own or with your facilitator or with the group.

groups.name: Your body
groups.line: Moving it, making it strong, and what it can do in water.

groups.name: The outdoors
groups.line: Fire, weather, wild things, and everything above your head.

groups.name: Your mind
groups.line: Numbers, words, memory, seeing properly, and saying what you mean.

groups.name: Making things
groups.line: With your hands, with a tune, and with a bit of misdirection.

groups.name: Everyday life
groups.line: Feeding people, earning, fixing, caring, and keeping your head.

categories.name: Body and movement
categories.line: Juggling, skipping, upside down, breath, strength, speed.

tracks.name: Juggling
tracks.line: Three balls in the air, eventually.

steps.test: Throw one ball from hand to hand ten times without dropping it.
how: One ball only. A rolled sock works.
Throw it from your right hand to your left, up to about eye height.
Aim for the same arc every time rather than for speed.

steps.test: Throw one ball twenty times, and have every throw peak at the same height.
steps.note: Pick a spot on the wall at eye height. Every throw should touch it. Boring, and it is the whole thing.

steps.test: Throw one ball twenty times with your eyes on the top of the arc, not on your hands.
steps.note: You catch by feel, not by looking. This is the step that makes three balls possible later.

steps.test: Throw one ball twenty times starting with your weaker hand.
steps.note: Whichever hand you have been avoiding. Both hands have to learn this or three balls never comes.

steps.test: Do the two-ball exchange five times, drops allowed.
steps.note: One ball in each hand. Throw the right; when it reaches the top, throw the left. Catch what you can. Drops are expected here.

steps.test: Do the two-ball exchange ten times in a row, catching both.
Do the two-ball exchange twenty times, starting with your weaker hand.
Do the two-ball exchange twenty times without your feet moving.
steps.note: If you are chasing the balls, the throws are going forward. Throw straight up in front of your face instead.

steps.test: Hold three balls, throw all three once, and catch at least one.
steps.note: It will go everywhere. That is the step. Everybody looks foolish here and everybody gets through it.

steps.test: Do a three-ball cascade for three catches.
steps.note: A cascade means they cross over in the middle, not round in a circle.

steps.test: Do a three-ball cascade for five catches.
Do a three-ball cascade for ten catches.
Do a three-ball cascade for twenty catches.
Juggle three balls for thirty seconds with no drop.
Practise for ten minutes without stopping, however many times you drop them.
steps.note: Ten minutes on the clock. Pick them up and carry on. Everybody who can juggle dropped several hundred times first.

steps.test: Juggle three balls for a full minute.
Juggle three balls for two whole minutes.
Juggle two balls in one hand, twenty throws.
steps.note: Both balls in the SAME hand, going round in a circle. Harder than the cascade — a flourish, not a step backwards.

steps.test: Juggle while walking twenty steps.
Teach somebody their first ten throws, until they can do it without you.

tracks.name: Skipping
tracks.line: Stepping over a rope to running a game of it.

steps.test: Step over a rope lying still on the ground, ten times.
Swing the rope over your head and let it land in front of your feet, ten times.
steps.note: No jumping yet. Just get the rope round and stop it there.

steps.test: Swing it over and step across it, ten times.
Skip three times in a row.
Skip ten times in a row without stopping.
Skip twenty-five in a row.
Skip for one whole minute, however many times you trip.
Skip fifty in a row.
Skip one hundred in a row.
Skip ten times on one foot, then ten on the other.
Skip one hundred with the rope crossed over at least once.
Run a skipping game for other people.

tracks.name: Upside down
tracks.line: Rolls, cartwheels, handstands.

steps.test: Do a forward roll and come back up on your feet.
Do three forward rolls in a row, in a straight line.
Do a backward roll.
Kick your legs up against a wall and hold for five seconds.
steps.note: Hands a little way from the wall, arms straight, look at the floor between them.

steps.test: Hold a wall handstand for fifteen seconds.
Hold a wall handstand for thirty seconds.
Do a cartwheel, any shape at all, and land on your feet.
Do a cartwheel with your legs straight.
Cartwheel cleanly in both directions.
Walk your feet up a wall until your chest touches it, and hold for ten seconds.
Come out of a handstand into a roll, on purpose.
steps.note: Learn the way out before you need it. This is the step that makes the rest safe.

steps.test: Kick up away from the wall and hold for one second.
Hold a free handstand for three seconds.
Hold a free handstand for five seconds.
Hold a free handstand for ten seconds.
Hold ten seconds three separate times in one go.
Take one step on your hands.
Walk three steps on your hands.
Walk five steps on your hands.
Show somebody how to kick up safely, and hold their legs while they try.

tracks.name: Breath
tracks.line: Thirty seconds to two minutes, calmly.

steps.test: Hold your breath for thirty seconds, sitting still.
how: Sit down first. Never do this in water.
Breathe out all the way, then take one big slow breath in.
Hold, and stay still — moving uses it up.
Somebody counts to thirty out loud. Let it go whenever you want to.

steps.test: Breathe in for four, hold four, out for four, ten rounds.
Breathe out for twice as long as you breathe in, twenty times.
Hold your breath for forty-five seconds.
Take ten slow breaths through your nose only, with your mouth shut.
Hold your breath for one minute.
Slow your own heart down on purpose and notice it happen.
steps.note: Sit still, breathe out for longer than you breathe in, and feel your pulse at your wrist. It slows.

steps.test: Hold your breath for seventy-five seconds.
Breathe yourself calm before something you are nervous about.
Hold your breath for ninety seconds.
Hold your breath for two minutes.
Teach somebody the slow breathing until they can do it without you.

tracks.name: Strength
tracks.line: One press-up to carrying somebody.

steps.test: Do one press-up properly, all the way down and up.
Do five press-ups without stopping.
Do ten press-ups without stopping.
Carry a full bag in each hand the length of the street.
Hang from a bar for thirty seconds.
Pick something heavy up off the floor with a straight back, ten times.
steps.note: Legs, not back. Get this habit before the weights get real.

steps.test: Hang from a bar for sixty seconds.
Carry something heavy and awkward up a full flight of stairs.
Do twenty press-ups without stopping.
Hold a plank for two minutes.
Carry something heavy in each hand for a hundred metres without setting it down.
Do one pull-up from a dead hang.
Do thirty press-ups without stopping.
Carry a younger child on your back across a field.
Do five pull-ups.
Do forty press-ups without stopping.
Carry somebody your own size ten metres.
Carry somebody your own size twenty-five metres.
Carry somebody your own size fifty metres.
Help somebody move house for a whole day, and still be useful at the end of it.

tracks.name: Running
tracks.line: A hundred metres to an hour.

steps.test: Run one hundred metres flat out.
Run for one minute without stopping.
Run for three minutes without stopping.
Run for five minutes without stopping.
Go running three times in one week.
Run for eight minutes without stopping.
Run for ten minutes without stopping.
Run a mile without walking any of it.
Go out and run in the rain, on purpose, and finish.
Run for fifteen minutes without stopping.
Run three times a week for a fortnight.
Run for twenty minutes without stopping.
Run two miles without walking.
Run up a hill without walking any of it.
Run for twenty-five minutes without stopping.
Run for thirty minutes without stopping.
Run four miles.
Run five kilometres without stopping.
Run five kilometres faster than the first time you did it.
Run beside somebody doing their first mile, and finish at their pace.

tracks.name: Balance
tracks.line: A log to a slackline.

steps.test: Walk the length of a log or a low wall without falling off.
Stand on one foot for thirty seconds.
steps.twist: The foot you would never choose.

steps.test: Stand on one foot for a full minute.
steps.twist: The foot you would never choose.

steps.test: Stand on one foot for thirty seconds with your eyes closed.
steps.note: Much harder than it sounds. Balance is mostly your eyes until you train the rest.

steps.test: Stand on one foot for a minute with your eyes closed.
Walk heel to toe along a straight line for twenty steps.
Walk heel to toe for twenty steps with your eyes closed.
Walk a kerb the length of a street without stepping off.
Stand on one foot and pick something up off the floor.
steps.twist: The foot you would never choose.

steps.test: Go down on one leg holding something, and stand back up.
Stand up on a slackline or a beam and stay there for ten seconds.
Stand on it for thirty seconds.
Take three steps along it.
Walk two metres along it.
Walk five metres along it.
Stop halfway, stand still for five seconds, and carry on.
Kneel down on it and stand back up.
Turn round on it.
Turn round on it and come back.
Hold somebody steady while they cross theirs for the first time.

tracks.name: Riding
tracks.line: Balance bike to a long road.

steps.test: Sit on a bike and push yourself along with your feet.
Push off and freewheel with both feet up for three seconds.
Freewheel for ten seconds, steering as you go.
Ride ten metres pedalling, with nobody holding on.
Start off on your own from standing still.
Stop exactly where you meant to stop, three times.
Steer around three things without putting a foot down.
Ride up a hill without getting off.
Look over your shoulder and keep riding straight.
steps.note: This is the one that keeps you alive on a road. Practise it somewhere with no traffic.

steps.test: Signal with one hand and keep riding straight.
Ride two miles without stopping.
Ride on a road with the signals and the road sense, with an adult beside you.

tracks.name: Hopping and balancing
tracks.line: From four, beside you. One foot, two feet, a straight line and a roll.

steps.test: Stand on one foot while somebody counts to five. Then the other foot.
Stand on one foot while they count to ten.
Hop three times on one foot.
steps.twist: The foot you would never choose.

steps.test: Hop five times on one foot without putting the other one down.
steps.twist: The foot you would never choose.

steps.test: Jump with both feet together, ten times.
Jump over a line with both feet together, ten times.
Jump off a low step and land on two feet without wobbling.
Walk along a line without stepping off it.
Walk along the line heel to toe.
Do a forward roll on something soft.
Hop all the way across the room on one foot.
steps.twist: The foot you would never choose.

steps.test: Hop across the room, swap feet halfway, and land the last one still.
steps.twist: Start on the foot you would never choose.

categories.name: Outdoors and wild
categories.line: Fire, finding your way, shelter, weather, tracks, wild food.

tracks.name: Fire
tracks.line: Gathering sticks to teaching somebody else.

steps.test: Gather a bundle of dry sticks that would actually burn.
steps.note: Snap them. If they bend instead of snapping they are wet and they will not light.

steps.test: Gather three sizes: tinder, kindling, and wood, in three piles.
Lay a fire properly so that it would light.
Light it with matches, first go.
Put it out so completely that nobody could tell it was there.
steps.note: Water, stir, water again, and feel it with your hand. Warm is not out.

steps.test: Keep one going for half an hour without it needing rescuing.
Light one in the wind.
Cook something on a fire you laid and lit.
Light one with a single match.
Light one with a spark and no flame — a striker or a flint.
Light one when everything around you is damp.
Teach two other people to lay and light one safely.

tracks.name: Finding your way
tracks.line: Pointing north to leading a route.

steps.test: Point which way is north, and be right.
Name three landmarks you can see and say which way home is.
Find north from the sun, and check it against a compass.
Hold a map the right way round for where you are standing.
steps.note: Turn the map, not your head. Almost everybody gets lost because they never do this.

steps.test: Point out three things on the map that you can see in front of you.
Follow a marked path on a map for a mile without being told.
Read the contours and say which way the ground rises.
Walk to a spot you picked on the map and arrive at it.
Take a bearing with a compass and walk it for two hundred metres.
Walk a bearing to something you cannot see from the start.
Navigate a mile with a map and a compass.
Work out how long a walk will take before you set off, and be close.
Navigate three miles across country.
Find your way in poor visibility, slowly and safely.
Say where you are on the map at any moment, all the way round a walk.
Plan a route yourself, on paper, with the timings.
Lead the group along it and get everybody there.
Change the route halfway because of the weather, and say why.
Leave a route plan with somebody at home before you go.
Lead a route that takes a whole day, and bring everybody back on time.

tracks.name: Shelter
tracks.line: A den to a night out in it.

steps.test: Build a den big enough to sit inside.
Build one that two people fit in.
Choose a spot properly — not in a dip, not under a dead branch.
Build one with a frame that stands up on its own.
Thatch it so that daylight barely gets through.
Build one that keeps you dry through ten minutes of rain.
Get the door out of the wind, and say how you knew where the wind was.
Insulate the floor so the ground does not take your heat.
steps.note: The ground steals more warmth than the air does. This one step is the difference between a night and a miserable night.

steps.test: Build one you would be warm in overnight, and prove it with a thermometer.
Sit in your own shelter for two hours in bad weather.
Sleep a whole night in a shelter you built.
Build one with a group and get everybody through the night dry.

tracks.name: Weather and tide
tracks.line: Reading the day before it happens.

steps.test: Dress yourself right for the weather that is actually outside.
Read a forecast and say what everybody should bring.
Look at the sky and say whether the forecast looks right.
Know what wind chill is and dress for it, not for the number.
Pack a bag for a day out where the weather might turn.
Read a tide table and say when the beach will be gone.
Know which way the tide is going right now, by looking.
Plan a beach walk around the tide and get it right.
Say what time it gets dark today, without looking it up.
Plan a walk that finishes before dark, and finish before dark.
Spot weather coming in and say how long you have.
Turn back early, on purpose, and be glad you did.
Change or call off a plan because of the weather, and explain why.
steps.note: Calling it off is the hardest and most useful of these. Anybody can go anyway.

steps.test: Get somebody warm and dry again who got cold and wet.
Know the signs of somebody getting too cold, and what to do first.
Carry the right kit for the day without carrying everything.
Lead a short walk in weather that was not ideal, and keep it cheerful.
Read a shipping or mountain forecast and say what it means for tomorrow.
Make the call on a day out for other people, and be right.
Keep a group safe and cheerful through genuinely bad weather.

tracks.name: Trees and birds
tracks.line: Five leaves to leading a nature walk.

steps.test: Find five different kinds of leaf and lay them out.
Name three trees from their leaves alone.
Name five trees from their leaves alone.
Name three trees in winter, with no leaves on them at all.
Find the oldest tree near you and say how you can tell.
Name three birds on sight, outdoors, not from a book.
Sit still outside for ten minutes and count how many birds come.
Name five birds on sight.
Name three birds from their call with your eyes shut.
Name ten birds on sight.
Name ten birds from their call with your eyes shut.
Name ten wild plants where you walk.
Say which month each of five plants flowers, and be there when one does.
Name twenty wild plants and say which are useful.
Find a nest, a burrow or a den without disturbing it.
Keep a list of everything you name for a whole month.
Notice one thing changing with the season and follow it for a month.
Name what lives in one hedge, top to bottom.
Take one person out and name ten things for them.
Lead a walk and name what you pass as you go.

tracks.name: Wild food
tracks.line: One berry to a whole meal.

steps.test: Pick and eat one wild food with somebody who knows it.
steps.note: Never eat anything on this ladder without a person who is certain. Certain, not fairly sure.

steps.test: Learn the rule: if you are not certain, you do not eat it.
Identify one safe wild food on your own and have it checked.
Identify three safe wild foods without being told.
Name three things near you that would poison you, and how to know them.
Learn which of them has a lookalike, and what tells them apart.
Pick enough of something to bring home.
Wash it, prepare it and cook it.
Pick only what you need and leave the rest standing.
Find out whose land you are on and whether you may pick there.
Identify six safe wild foods without being told.
Name five things that would poison you, and why.
Follow one plant through a season until it is ready.
Pick something in each of three different months.
Make a meal where one ingredient came from the wild.
Make a meal where three ingredients came from the wild.
Preserve something you picked so it keeps.
Give some of what you picked to somebody else.
Say no to something you were not sure about, out loud.
Take somebody else foraging and keep them safe.

tracks.name: Tracking
tracks.line: A footprint to following an animal.

steps.test: Find an animal footprint and say what made it.
Find your own footprint and say which way you were going.
Follow your own tracks backwards for fifty metres.
Find three different sets of prints in one place.
Name three animals from their prints.
Find a run or a path an animal uses regularly.
Name three animals from their droppings.
Find where something has been eating, and say what it was.
Name five animals from their prints or droppings.
Say whether a track is fresh or old, and why you think so.
Follow an animal trail for a hundred metres.
Follow one for two hundred metres.
Read a trail and say what the animal was doing.
Read one and say roughly when it passed.
Find a print, make a cast of it, and keep it.
Sit still outdoors for twenty minutes without moving.
Sit still for forty minutes and write down everything that happened.
Move through woodland without being heard for fifty metres.
Sit still long enough that a wild animal comes close on its own.
Take somebody out and find them a track they can read themselves.

tracks.name: Camping
tracks.line: The garden to a wild night.

steps.test: Sleep a whole night in a tent in the garden.
Put a tent up with somebody helping.
Put a tent up on your own.
Take it down, dry it and pack it properly.
Pack for a night away from a list and forget nothing.
Choose a pitch — flat, dry, out of the wind — and say why.
Camp a night away from the house and cook your own tea.
Keep everything you own dry through a wet night.
Leave a pitch so that nobody could tell you were there.
Camp a night carrying everything you need on your back.
Camp two nights carrying everything you need.
Take a younger child on their first night out and get them home happy.

categories.name: Water and boats
categories.line: Swimming, cold water, rowing, sailing, fishing, rock pools.

tracks.name: Swimming
tracks.line: Face in the water to open water.

steps.test: Put your face in the water and blow bubbles, ten times.
how: Somebody who can already swim stays beside you for every step of this.
Face in, breathe out through your nose and mouth, come up.
Ten times. Do not hurry it.

steps.test: Hold the side and kick your legs for thirty seconds.
Push off the side and glide with your face in, as far as you can.
Float on your front for five seconds and stand back up.
Float on your back for ten seconds.
steps.note: This one is worth more than it looks. A person who can float on their back is a person who does not panic.

steps.test: Push off and glide with a leg kick, three metres.
Swim five metres any way you like, without touching the bottom.
Swim ten metres on your front.
Swim ten metres on your back.
Turn your head to the side, take one breath, and keep swimming.
Swim ten metres taking a breath every three or four strokes.
Jump in from the side and swim back to it.
Swim fifteen metres without stopping.
Pick something up off the bottom in water up to your chest.
Tread water for thirty seconds.
Tread water for a full minute.
Swim twenty-five metres on your front without stopping.
Swim twenty-five metres on your back without stopping.
Swim there and back with one rest in the middle.
Swim fifty metres without stopping, and climb out unaided.

tracks.warn: Never on your own, and never in open water on this ladder. Every step happens at a pool or a lifeguarded beach with somebody beside you who can already swim.

tracks.name: Cold water
tracks.line: Ankles to a proper dip.

steps.test: Stand in the sea up to your ankles for one minute.
steps.note: Never on your own, and never where you cannot get straight back out.

steps.test: Stand in up to your knees for a minute.
Get in up to your waist and stay calm.
Finish a shower with thirty seconds of cold.
Get in up to your shoulders and control your breathing.
steps.note: The gasp is normal and it passes in about a minute. Long slow breaths out.

steps.test: Finish a shower with a full minute of cold, three days running.
Stay in up to your shoulders for one minute.
Stay in for two minutes and get warm again properly afterwards.
steps.note: Warm clothes and a hot drink ready before you go in. Getting warm again is half the skill.

steps.test: Go in on a day you did not feel like it.
Do it once a week for a month, whatever the weather.
Stay in for four minutes.
Take somebody else through their first cold dip safely.

tracks.name: Rowing and paddling
tracks.line: Getting in to crossing a lough.

steps.test: Get into a boat and sit safely without wobbling it.
Put a buoyancy aid on properly and check somebody else's.
Move a boat twenty metres under your own power.
Move it in a straight line for a hundred metres.
Steer around a marker and come back.
Stop the boat where you meant to stop it.
Turn it round on the spot.
Come alongside a jetty and get out without help.
Paddle one kilometre.
Paddle into the wind for ten minutes and keep your line.
Paddle five kilometres with a group.
Take a beginner out and bring them back confident.

tracks.name: Sailing
tracks.line: Naming the parts to sailing a course.

steps.test: Name the parts of a small boat and what each one does.
Put a buoyancy aid on properly and say what you would do if you went in.
Say which way the wind is coming from, without being told.
Rig a small boat and check it over before it goes in.
Sit in the right place and hold the tiller and the rope at once.
Sail a straight line across the wind.
Sail out and come back to where you started.
Let the sail out and pull it in to change your speed on purpose.
Tack — turn through the wind — without stopping.
Tack three times in a row and keep going.
Gybe safely, with your head down.
Sail a triangle around three marks.
Sail in a stronger wind and stay in control.
Right a capsized dinghy and get back in.
steps.note: Everybody capsizes. Doing it on purpose, with somebody watching, is how it stops being frightening.

steps.test: Sail a full course with buoys.
Come alongside and stop the boat exactly where you wanted.
Take somebody out as your crew and tell them what to do.
Crew properly for somebody else and be useful.
Sail a race, wherever you finish.
Take somebody on their first ever sail and hand them the tiller.

tracks.name: Fishing
tracks.line: A rock pool to your own supper.

steps.test: Catch something in a rock pool with a net and put it back.
Set up a rod with a line and a hook, on your own.
Tie the knot that holds the hook on, three times, until it holds.
Cast and land the line roughly where you meant it to go.
Cast ten times and land eight of them where you aimed.
Sit and fish for a whole hour without needing anything to happen.
steps.note: This is the part of fishing that is actually fishing.

steps.test: Find out what is legal to catch where you are, and when.
Catch a fish.
Get the hook out and put a fish back unharmed.
Catch three in one outing.
Catch, prepare and cook a fish you caught.
Teach somebody else to cast and land one.

tracks.name: Rock pools and shore
tracks.line: Five creatures to reading the shore.

steps.test: Find five different creatures in a rock pool.
Name five of them correctly.
Turn a stone over, look under it, and put it back the way it was.
Explain what the tide does to everything living there.
Find the high tide line and say how you know.
Find and name ten seashore species.
Do a proper shore survey and write down what you found.
Lead a rock pool hunt for younger children.

categories.name: Fitness and strength
categories.line: Press-ups, sit-ups, pull-ups, the plank, lifting, sprinting.

tracks.name: Press-ups
tracks.line: Two, up to fifty.

steps.test: Do two proper press-ups. Knees on the floor is fine.
steps.note: Proper means chest to the floor and arms straight at the top. Two good ones beat ten bad ones.

steps.test: Do five with your knees on the floor.
Do ten with your knees on the floor.
Do one with your knees off the floor.
Do five with your knees off the floor.
Do eight in one go.
Do ten in one go.
Do press-ups on three separate days in one week.
Do fifteen in one go.
Do twenty in one go.
Do fifty across one day, in as many sets as you like.
Do twenty-five in one go.
Do five slowly, three seconds down and three seconds up.
Do thirty in one go.
Do press-ups every other day for a fortnight.
Do thirty-five in one go.
Do forty in one go.
Do a hundred across one day.
Do fifty in one go.
Get somebody else from none to their first proper one.

tracks.name: Sit-ups
tracks.line: Five, up to a hundred.

steps.test: Do five sit-ups.
Do ten without stopping.
Do fifteen without stopping.
Hold yourself halfway up for twenty seconds.
Do twenty without stopping.
Do sit-ups on three separate days in one week.
Do thirty without stopping.
Do ten slowly, three seconds up and three seconds down.
Do forty without stopping.
Do fifty without stopping.
Lie down and lift both straight legs to vertical, ten times.
Do sixty without stopping.
Do a hundred across one day, in as many sets as you like.
Do seventy without stopping.
Hang from a bar and lift your knees to your chest, ten times.
Do eighty without stopping.
Do sit-ups every other day for a fortnight.
Do a hundred without stopping.
Do a hundred in under four minutes.
Do a hundred in under three minutes.

tracks.name: Pull-ups
tracks.line: Hanging on, up to ten.

steps.test: Hang from a bar with your feet off the ground for ten seconds.
Hang for twenty seconds.
Hang for thirty seconds.
Hang and pull your shoulders down away from your ears, five times.
steps.note: Arms stay straight. Only the shoulders move. This is the muscle that starts a pull-up.

steps.test: Do five rows under a low bar or a table, feet on the floor.
steps.note: Lie under it, grab it, pull your chest up to it. Feet on the floor takes most of your weight.

steps.test: Do ten rows.
Do fifteen rows.
Jump to the top of a pull-up and hold your chin over the bar for five seconds.
Hold your chin over the bar for ten seconds.
Jump to the top and lower yourself as slowly as you can, three times.
Lower yourself over a slow count of five, three times.
steps.note: Lowering slowly is where the strength is built. Almost everybody who gets a first pull-up got it from these.

steps.test: Lower yourself over a count of five, five times, on three days in one week.
Do a pull-up with one foot resting on a chair, five times.
Do a pull-up with a band, or with somebody holding your feet, five times.
Do one pull-up on your own, chin over the bar.
Do one pull-up on three separate days in one week.
Do two in a row.
Do three in a row.
Do five across a day, in singles.
Do four in a row, and show somebody the slow lowering.

tracks.name: The plank
tracks.line: Twenty seconds, up to five minutes.

steps.test: Hold a plank for twenty seconds without your hips dropping.
steps.note: A straight line from your head to your heels. If your hips sag it is not a plank, it is a rest.

steps.test: Hold it for thirty seconds.
Hold it for forty-five seconds.
Hold it for one minute.
Hold it three separate times in one go, a minute each.
Hold a side plank for twenty seconds on each side.
Hold it for ninety seconds.
Hold it for two minutes.
Hold a side plank for a minute on each side.
Hold it for three minutes.
Hold a side plank for two minutes on each side.
Hold a plank for five minutes.

tracks.name: Squats
tracks.line: Ten, up to one on one leg.

steps.test: Do ten squats with your heels staying flat on the floor.
steps.note: Heels down is the whole thing. If they lift, go less deep until they stay.

steps.test: Do twenty in one go.
Sit at the bottom of a squat for thirty seconds.
Do thirty in one go.
Do squats on three separate days in one week.
Do fifty in one go.
Sit at the bottom of a squat for a full minute.
Do ten slowly, four seconds down and four seconds up.
Do seventy in one go.
Do twenty holding something heavy.
Do a hundred in one go.
Do a hundred across one day, split however you like.
Do ten jump squats, landing quietly.
Do thirty holding something heavy.
Stand on one leg and go down as far as you can, holding a chair.
steps.twist: The leg you would never choose first.

steps.test: Go halfway down on one leg without holding anything.
steps.twist: The leg you would never choose first.

steps.test: Go down on one leg to a low seat and stand back up.
Do one squat on one leg, all the way down and back up.
Do three on one leg, on both legs.
Do a hundred and fifty across one day, and still walk properly the next.

tracks.name: Lifting
tracks.line: Picking it up right, to carrying a person.

steps.test: Pick something heavy up with your legs, back straight, and put it down again.
steps.note: Feet under it, back flat, knees bend, chest up. Get the shape right while it is light.

steps.test: Do that ten times without your back rounding once.
Carry something heavy fifty metres without putting it down.
Lift something the weight of your own head straight overhead.
Carry something awkward — a box, a bag of sand — up a flight of stairs.
Carry something heavy in each hand for a hundred metres.
Lift something and put it on a high shelf without wobbling.
Carry something half your own weight two hundred metres.
Move ten heavy things with somebody, taking the awkward end each time.
Lift something heavy from the floor to your shoulder in one go.
Carry your own bodyweight fifty metres.
Help somebody move house for a whole day and still be useful at the end.

tracks.name: Bending and stretching
tracks.line: Past your knees, to the splits.

steps.test: Reach past your knees with your legs straight.
Stretch for five minutes every morning for five days running.
Reach your shins with your legs straight.
Sit on the floor with your legs straight and reach your ankles.
Hold a hamstring stretch for a full minute on each leg.
steps.note: A full minute. Thirty seconds is where most people stop and it is where the change starts.

steps.test: Touch your toes with your knees slightly bent.
Hold a deep squat with your heels down for thirty seconds.
Hold the deep squat for a full minute.
Reach one hand over your shoulder and the other up your back, and touch your fingers.
Do the same with the other arm on top.
steps.note: One side will be much worse than the other. That side is the point of this step.

steps.test: Stretch every day for two weeks without missing one.
Touch your toes with your legs straight.
Hold your toes for thirty seconds with your legs straight.
Put your knuckles on the floor with your legs straight.
Sit with your legs wide and lean forward until your elbows reach the floor.
Lie on your back and pull one straight leg up until it points at the ceiling.
Kneel, lean back and hold your heels for twenty seconds.
Put both palms flat on the floor with your knees a little bent.
Hold a bridge — hands and feet down, hips up — for twenty seconds.
Put both palms flat on the floor with your legs straight, and hold it for ten seconds.

tracks.name: Sprinting
tracks.line: Ten seconds flat out, to a real race.

steps.test: Sprint flat out for ten seconds.
Sprint ten seconds, walk a minute, and do it five times.
Run a hundred metres without slowing down at the end.
steps.note: Almost everybody eases off in the last twenty. Do not.

steps.test: Time your hundred metres and write the number down.
Beat that time.
Sprint uphill five times.
Run a hundred metres in under twenty seconds.
Sprint from a standing start ten times, resting properly between.
Run a hundred metres in under eighteen seconds.
Sprint three separate days in one week.
Run a hundred metres in under sixteen seconds.
Race somebody who beat you before, and beat your own old time doing it.

categories.name: Air and sky
categories.line: Kites, rockets, planes, stars, weather in the sky.

tracks.name: Kites
tracks.line: Flying one to making one that flies.

steps.test: Get a kite into the air and keep it there for a minute.
Work out which way the wind is going before you launch.
Launch it on your own, with nobody holding it.
Land it on your own without it crashing.
Fly it for ten minutes without it coming down.
Make a kite from scratch that actually flies.
Change one thing about it — the tail, the bridle — and fly it better.
Teach two younger children to launch and land.

tracks.name: Rockets
tracks.line: A bottle rocket to a two-stage one.

steps.test: Make a paper rocket and launch it off a straw.
Make three with different fins and see which goes furthest.
Make a water bottle rocket that leaves the ground.
Launch it safely — everybody back, nobody over it.
steps.note: A pressurised bottle is a real thing. Set the rules before the first launch, every time.

steps.test: Get one ten metres up, measured.
Change one thing, test it, and say whether it helped.
Get one twenty metres up, measured.
Work out how much water gives the best flight, by trying it.
Build one with a nose cone that stays on.
Build one with a parachute that comes back down safely.
Launch three in a row that all work.
Run a rocket launch afternoon for other people.

tracks.name: Stars and planets
tracks.line: One constellation to knowing the sky.

steps.test: Find the Plough and the North Star.
Use the Plough to find north, and check it against a compass.
Name three constellations and find them on your own.
Go out on a clear night and just look up for ten minutes.
Find Orion, and the three stars of his belt.
Find Cassiopeia.
Tell the difference between a star and a planet by eye.
steps.note: Stars twinkle. Planets hold steady. Once you have seen it you cannot unsee it.

steps.test: Find a planet with your own eyes and know which one it is.
Watch the moon on five nights and draw what it looked like.
Know what the moon will look like tomorrow, and be right.
Spot a satellite crossing the sky.
Find the Milky Way from somewhere dark.
Watch a meteor shower and count what you see.
Find five constellations without help.
Look at the moon through binoculars and find one crater.
Find the Andromeda galaxy.
Know which constellations belong to which season, and say why they move.
Find eight constellations without help.
Take somebody out and show them three things in the sky.
Run a stargazing night and show people what is up there.

tracks.name: Things that fly
tracks.line: Paper wings to something with a motor.

steps.test: Fold a paper aeroplane that flies across the room.
Fold three different ones and see which flies furthest.
Fold one that flies ten metres, measured.
Bend the back edge of the wings up a little and see what it does.
steps.note: Those are elevators. You have just found out how a real aeroplane is steered.

steps.test: Make one that turns in a circle on purpose.
Fold one that flies thirty feet, measured, with somebody watching.
Make one that glides slowly instead of fast, and say why it does.
Explain what keeps an aeroplane up, in your own words.
Build a card or balsa glider from a plan.
Get it to fly level instead of diving, by moving the weight.
Make it fly twenty metres.
Build a glider of your own design that flies.
Make a paper helicopter and time how long it takes to fall.
Change the blades and make it fall slower.
Build something with elastic or a motor that leaves the ground.
Get it to fly the same way twice.
Fly something with a controller and land it on purpose.
Fly it round a marker and back.
Build or fly a small helicopter or drone that lifts and lands where you meant.
Run a flying afternoon and get everybody something in the air.

tracks.name: Wind and weather watching
tracks.line: Which way to keeping records.

steps.test: Say which way the wind is blowing without looking at anything.
Say roughly how hard it is blowing, and check it against a forecast.
Make something that shows wind direction and put it up outside.
Watch it for a week and write down which way the wind came from each day.
Name three cloud types on sight.
Name five cloud types on sight.
Say what each of those five usually means for the next few hours.
Spot rain coming before anybody else does, and be right.
Predict tomorrow from the sky alone, and check whether you were right.
Do that on five days and count how many you got.
Explain what a front is, and spot one arriving.
Read a pressure reading and say what it means.
Keep a weather record every day for a fortnight.
Keep it every day for a month.
Work out from your own record which wind brings the rain here.
Get three forecasts right in a row and explain how.
Know when the sun sets today without looking it up, to within ten minutes.
Call the weather for a day out, and be right enough that nobody got caught.
Get five forecasts right in a row and explain how.
Teach somebody to read the sky well enough that they get one right.

tracks.name: Throwing
tracks.line: Hitting a target to hitting it every time.

steps.test: Scrunch a sheet of paper into a ball and throw it into a bin from five paces.
Do that five times out of five.
Hit a target the size of a bin lid from ten paces.
Hit it five times out of five.
Hit it from twenty paces.
Throw with your other hand and hit it from five paces.
Throw something as far as you can, then beat it by five metres.
steps.twist: Other hand, then beat that too.

steps.test: Catch ten in a row thrown at you.
Skim a stone three bounces.
Skim a stone six bounces.
Skim one ten bounces.
Teach somebody else to skim one properly.

categories.name: Mind and numbers
categories.line: Tables, the cube, chess, memory, codes, puzzles.

tracks.name: Times tables
tracks.line: Counting in twos to sixty seconds flat.

steps.test: Count in twos up to twenty.
Count in fives up to fifty, and in tens up to a hundred.
Say the two times table with no mistakes.
Say the five and ten times tables with no mistakes.
Say the three times table.
Say the four times table.
Answer twenty mixed questions from the tables you know, all correct.
Say the six times table.
Say the seven times table.
Say the eight times table.
Say the nine times table, and spot the trick in it.
steps.note: Add the two digits of any answer in the nine times table. They come to nine every time.

steps.test: Say the eleven and twelve times tables.
Say every table up to twelve correctly, with no time limit.
Answer thirty mixed questions in a row, all correct.
Say every table up to twelve in under three minutes.
Answer any single table question in under two seconds.
Say every table up to twelve in under two minutes.
Say every table up to twelve in under ninety seconds.
Say every table up to twelve in under sixty seconds.
Teach somebody else one whole table until they have it.

tracks.name: The cube
tracks.line: One face to under a minute.

steps.test: Name the pieces and turn the cube twenty times without losing track of a colour.
steps.note: Centres never move. Whatever colour is in the middle is that face, always.

steps.test: Learn what the letters mean — R, L, U, D, F, B — and turn each one.
Follow a written sequence of six turns without a mistake.
Make one whole face a single colour, with nobody helping you.
Solve the white cross — four white edges round the white centre.
Solve the white cross with the sides matching their centres too.
Put one white corner in, on your own.
Solve the whole white layer, corners and all.
Solve the white layer again in under two minutes.
Learn the sequence that puts a middle edge in to the right.
Learn the one that puts it in to the left.
Solve the middle layer.
Solve the first two layers three times in a row.
Learn the sequence for the yellow cross, and get it.
Get the yellow cross from any starting position.
Learn the sequence that puts the last corners in place.
Solve the whole cube with the sheet in front of you.
Solve the whole cube with nothing in front of you.
Solve it from three different scrambles in one sitting, under five minutes each.
Solve it in under three minutes, and teach somebody the white cross.

tracks.name: Chess
tracks.line: Setting the board to teaching a beginner.

steps.test: Set the board up correctly and name every piece.
steps.note: White square on the right, and the queen goes on her own colour.

steps.test: Know how every piece moves.
Play one full game to the end.
Castle, and say why you did it.
Take a piece with a pawn the way pawns actually take.
Say the value of each piece and stop giving them away for nothing.
Play five whole games in one week.
Checkmate with a queen and a king against a lone king.
Checkmate with only a king and a rook.
Spot a fork before you play into one.
Win a game against somebody who is genuinely trying.
Open the same way three games running and notice what changes.
Get your pieces out and your king safe in the first ten moves, every time.
Solve ten mate-in-one puzzles.
Solve ten mate-in-two puzzles.
Play a whole game without losing a piece for nothing.
Win a game by a plan you had before it started.
Lose a game and say afterwards where it actually went wrong.
Beat an adult who plays properly.
Teach a complete beginner until they can play a full game.

tracks.name: Memory
tracks.line: Six digits to a hundred.

steps.test: Memorise a six-digit number and say it back a minute later.
Memorise a phone number and say it back an hour later.
Say your own address and two phone numbers from memory, with nothing in your hand.
Memorise a five-item shopping list and buy it with no list in your hand.
Learn the names of five people you met today, and use them tomorrow.
Turn five words into five daft pictures in your head, and say them back.
steps.note: The dafter the picture the better it sticks. That is not a trick, it is how memory actually works.

steps.test: Walk through your own house in your head and name ten places, in order.
steps.note: Front door, hall, kitchen. Always the same ten, always the same order. This is your memory palace.

steps.test: Put five things in those first five places, and say them back.
Put ten things in ten places, and say them back.
Say those same ten back the next morning.
Memorise twenty digits of pi.
Memorise a four-line verse, and say it a week later.
Memorise fifteen things in order.
Learn the first ten cards of a shuffled deck, in order.
Memorise thirty digits of pi.
Memorise twenty things in order.
Say that twenty back a full day later.
Learn twenty cards of a shuffled deck, in order.
Memorise fifty digits of pi.
Have somebody read you twenty things, and say them back in order, in front of them.

tracks.name: Mental arithmetic
tracks.line: Adding in your head to doing it fast.

steps.test: Add two single-digit numbers in your head, twenty in a row, correct.
Add and take away inside twenty, twenty in a row.
Add a two-digit number and a single digit, ten in a row.
Add two two-digit numbers in your head, five in a row.
Take one two-digit number from another, five in a row.
Round to the nearest ten and correct it afterwards.
steps.note: 47 + 38 is 47 + 40 minus 2. This one trick does most of the work for the rest of the ladder.

steps.test: Add three two-digit numbers in your head.
Double any two-digit number instantly.
Halve any two-digit number instantly.
Multiply a two-digit number by a single digit in your head.
Work out ten per cent of anything instantly.
Work out any percentage of a price in your head.
Multiply two two-digit numbers in your head.
Work out change from a note before the till tells you.
Add up a shopping basket as you go, and be within a pound at the till.
Work out a restaurant bill and the split, in your head, before anybody else.
Square any two-digit number ending in five.
steps.note: 35 squared: 3 times 4 is 12, then stick 25 on the end. 1225. It always works.

steps.test: Do ten mixed sums in your head in under a minute.
Beat a calculator user on ten easy sums.
Teach somebody one of these tricks until they can use it.

tracks.name: Codes and ciphers
tracks.line: A secret message to breaking one.

steps.test: Write a message in a shift cipher and have somebody read it.
Read one written for you, given the key.
Crack a shift cipher you were not given the key to.
Write a message backwards, and one in a simple substitution.
Count how often each letter appears in a page of English.
steps.note: E, then T, then A. That count is the crowbar for everything after this.

steps.test: Break a substitution cipher using letter frequency.
Use a keyword cipher properly.
Use a book cipher with somebody who has the same book.
Invent your own cipher that a friend cannot break in ten minutes.
Hide a message in plain sight so nobody notices it is a message.
Send and receive three messages nobody else read.
Run a treasure hunt for other people using codes.

tracks.name: Puzzles
tracks.line: A jigsaw to the hard stuff.

steps.test: Finish a twenty-four piece jigsaw on your own.
Finish a hundred-piece jigsaw on your own.
Finish an easy sudoku with no help.
Sit with a puzzle for twenty minutes without looking up the answer.
steps.note: Being stuck is not failing. It is the part where the thinking happens.

steps.test: Solve a wolf, goat and cabbage style riddle without being told.
Finish a medium sudoku.
Solve a lateral thinking puzzle by asking questions.
Finish a crossword, with help if you need it.
Finish a hard sudoku or a logic grid.
Solve a puzzle you had given up on the day before.
Solve a puzzle by working backwards from the answer.
Write a puzzle of your own that stumps three people.

tracks.name: Finding things out
tracks.line: Asking well, looking it up, checking it.

steps.test: Ask somebody a question you do not know the answer to, and get an answer you understand.
Ask a second question because the first answer was not enough.
Look something up on your own and explain it back to another person.
Find out how to do something you have never done, then do it the same day.
Ask an AI a question so clear that the first answer is actually useful.
Catch an answer that was wrong, and find out that it was.
steps.note: Everything answers confidently. Confident and right are different things.

steps.test: Check one fact in two different places and say which you trust more, and why.
Find who first said a thing everybody repeats.
Find the original of something, not somebody talking about it.
Ask the person who would actually know, rather than looking it up.
Change your mind about something because of what you found.
Teach somebody else how you go about finding things out.

tracks.name: Maps
tracks.line: Finding yourself to drawing one.

steps.test: Find where you are standing on a paper map.
Turn the map so it matches the ground in front of you.
Point out three things on the map that you can see in real life.
Work out how far away something is using the map scale.
Say how long that would take to walk.
Read the symbols and say what six of them mean.
Read the contours and pick the flattest way between two points.
Draw a map of your own street that somebody else can follow.
Draw a map of your area with a scale and a north arrow.
Read a timetable and plan a journey with a change in it.
Get yourself somewhere new using only a map and a timetable.
Plan a whole day out for other people on paper, and then run it.

categories.name: Words and languages
categories.line: A new language, reading, books, handwriting, poems, stories, signing.

tracks.name: A new language
tracks.line: One sentence to a real conversation.

steps.test: Learn one usable sentence and say it out loud to another person.
Say hello, please, thank you and goodbye, without thinking about it.
Count to ten out loud.
Say your own name, your age and where you live.
Learn twenty words you would actually use, and say them to somebody.
Ask one question, and understand the answer you get.
Count to a hundred.
Learn the words for ten things in the room you are sitting in.
Order a drink or a snack entirely in the language.
Learn fifty more words — food, family, the weather, the time.
Say five sentences about your own day.
Understand a whole sentence said to you at normal speed.
Watch five minutes of something in the language and catch ten words.
Ask for directions and follow the answer.
Learn the past tense of five common verbs, and use each one.
Tell somebody what you did yesterday, in three sentences.
Read a page written for children and understand most of it.
Have a two-minute exchange with somebody else who is learning it.
Have a five-minute conversation with somebody who speaks it well.
Order a meal, ask two questions and answer three about yourself — all with somebody who grew up speaking it.

tracks.name: Irish
tracks.line: Your own name to a conversation.

steps.test: Say your own name and where you are from, in Irish.
Say hello, goodbye, please and thank you.
Count to ten in Irish.
Learn the Irish for ten things in your house, and put a label on each.
Ask somebody how they are, and answer when they ask you.
Learn the days of the week.
Find out what your own town or townland name means in Irish.
steps.note: Almost every place name here is Irish underneath. Yours says something, and it is usually about the land.

steps.test: Learn what five place names near you mean, and tell somebody.
Count to a hundred.
Learn twenty words for food, and ask for something in Irish.
Say five sentences about your own day.
Understand a whole sentence said to you at normal speed.
Listen to five minutes of Irish radio or television and catch ten words.
Read a short piece written for children and understand most of it.
Learn the past tense of five common verbs, and use each one.
Tell somebody in Irish what you did yesterday.
Learn a song or a poem in Irish and say it from memory.
Have a two-minute conversation with somebody else who is learning.
Have a five-minute conversation with a fluent speaker.
Tell a short story in Irish to the group.

tracks.name: Reading
tracks.line: Letter sounds to reading aloud to the little ones.

steps.test: Know the sound every letter makes.
steps.note: The sound, not the name. B is 'buh'. Say it short — 'buh', not 'buhhh'.
how: Not the letter names — the sounds. B is 'buh', not 'bee'.
Go through the alphabet making the sound each letter makes.
Do it out loud with somebody who can tell you when it is off.

steps.test: Say the sounds in a three-letter word one at a time — c, a, t.
Push three sounds together and say the whole word.
Read ten three-letter words out loud.
Read a whole sentence made of three-letter words.
Read ten everyday words on sight — the, and, said, was.
Read twenty everyday words on sight.
Read a page of a first reading book out loud.
Learn the two-letter sounds — sh, ch, th, ck.
Read ten words with those sounds in them.
Read a whole first reading book out loud to somebody.
Read a book with a sentence on every page, on your own.
Read for five minutes with nobody helping.
Learn the long vowel sounds — ai, ee, igh, oa, oo.
Read twenty words with long vowel sounds in them.
Read a page and tell somebody what happened on it.
Read for ten minutes with nobody helping.
Read a whole short chapter on your own.
Read a whole short book on your own, over as many days as it takes.
Read a whole short book out loud to somebody younger, with no help.

tracks.name: Reading books
tracks.line: One page tonight to a whole book in a day.

steps.test: Read one page of a book tonight before you sleep.
Read ten pages in one sitting.
Read on three separate days in one week.
Read for twenty minutes without once picking up your phone.
steps.note: Phone in another room. Twenty minutes. That is the whole test.

steps.test: Finish a book you chose yourself. Any book, any length.
steps.note: Chose yourself matters. Nobody set it, nobody recommended it, you are not being examined on it.

steps.test: Read something every day for a week, even if it is one page.
Read for thirty minutes, count the pages, and write the number down.
steps.note: That number is your speed. Everything after this is measured against it.

steps.test: Ask somebody what you should read next, and start it that week.
steps.note: Not knowing what to read next is the commonest reason people stop. Ask somebody who reads.

steps.test: Read twenty-five pages in one sitting.
Read fifty pages in one day.
Read two books inside one month.
Read for a whole hour without stopping.
Read in three different places — outside, on a journey, and somewhere you never have.
Read a hundred pages in one day.
Finish a book you would have said was too hard for you.
Tell somebody what a book was about, well enough that they want to read it.
Read a hundred and fifty pages in one day.
Read every day for a month without missing a day.
Read a two-hundred-page book inside one day, in under eight hours of reading.
steps.note: A whole book between getting up and going to bed. It is an ordinary Saturday, and almost nobody believes it until they do it.

steps.test: Read a book a week for a month, and give one of them to somebody who needs it.

tracks.name: Writing by hand
tracks.line: Your name to something that changes a mind.

steps.test: Write your own name so anybody could read it.
Write the whole alphabet, upper and lower case, readably.
Write a sentence anybody can read.
Write ten lines and keep every letter the same height.
Write a full page that stays readable to the last line.
Write a thank-you note to somebody by hand.
Write a letter to a real person and post it.
Fill a page a day for a week.
Write two hundred words that somebody reads all the way through.
Write five hundred words in one sitting.
Write a thousand words that somebody finishes.
Write something by hand that changes somebody's mind.

tracks.name: Beautiful writing
tracks.line: Neat to genuinely lovely.

steps.test: Write the alphabet neatly, all the same size.
Rule guide lines and write on them without wandering off.
Hold a broad pen at one angle and keep it there for a whole line.
steps.note: The pen does the beauty. Your only job is not to twist it.

steps.test: Write ten letters that all lean the same way.
Copy a line of italic or copperplate that looks like the example.
Write the whole alphabet in one hand, evenly.
Write the capitals of that hand.
Space a word so that it looks even, and say what you changed.
Write a whole sentence with even spacing.
Write out a short quotation with no mistakes.
Write it again better, having seen what was wrong the first time.
Write a quotation beautifully enough to put on a wall.
Learn a second hand and write the alphabet in it.
Draw one large decorated letter.
Lay a page out — where the words sit, how much white is left.
Write somebody's name as a gift.
Address and decorate an envelope somebody keeps.
Write a card for an occasion that mattered.
Letter a sign or a poster other people actually use.
Show somebody how to hold the pen, and get them one good line.

tracks.name: Poems and lines
tracks.line: Four lines to running the evening.

steps.test: Learn a four-line rhyme and say it from memory.
Say it out loud to one other person.
Say eight lines from memory without a prompt.
Find a poem you actually like, on your own.
Learn sixteen lines.
Say twenty lines to a room, standing up.
Say it slowly enough that people hear the words.
steps.note: Everybody rushes. Half a second at the end of each line is the whole difference.

steps.test: Learn a whole poem, forty lines or more.
Write four lines of your own that mean something.
Write eight lines and read them to one person.
Perform your own to a room.
Run a poetry evening for other people.

tracks.name: Sign language
tracks.line: The alphabet to a conversation.

steps.test: Learn the sign-language alphabet for the letters of your name, and spell your name with your hands.
steps.note: Sign language has its own alphabet. Any short video of the British Sign Language alphabet will show you the letters.

steps.test: Finger-spell the whole alphabet.
Finger-spell somebody else's name and have them read it.
Learn ten everyday signs.
Learn twenty everyday signs.
Sign hello, please, thank you and sorry without thinking.
Ask a question in signs and understand the answer.
Learn the signs for your own family.
Learn forty signs.
Hold a one-minute conversation in signs.
Learn what your face and your body do in a signed sentence.
steps.note: The grammar is on your face. Signing with a blank face is like speaking in a flat monotone.

steps.test: Sign a whole verse of a song.
Learn sixty signs.
Hold a three-minute conversation.
Understand somebody signing at their own speed, not slowed down for you.
Sign a whole song or a poem.
Have a real conversation with somebody who signs.
Get through a whole conversation without needing to spell anything out.
Teach the group ten signs they remember a week later.
Be the one who includes somebody who signs, without being asked.

categories.name: Speaking and people
categories.line: Strangers, the stage, listening, hard things, humour, teaching.

tracks.name: Talking to people you do not know
tracks.line: Hello, to interviewing anybody.

steps.test: Say hello and your name to a child you have never met.
Say good morning to somebody passing, and mean it.
Ask somebody behind a counter a question, out loud, on your own.
Ask a stranger for the time or for directions.
Pay for something yourself and say thank you at the end.
Ask a shop assistant to find you something.
Walk into a cafe, ask for a table and order your own food.
Ask somebody a second question, because you were actually interested.
Learn one thing about somebody you did not know before, in a queue.
Start a conversation with somebody your own age you have never met.
Ask somebody at work what their job is actually like.
Write ten questions you would ask anybody.
Interview an adult with those ten questions.
Interview somebody you have never met and get a real answer.
Ask somebody about the thing they know most about, and keep them talking ten minutes.
Introduce two people who do not know each other.
Ring somewhere and ask a question on the telephone.
Go somewhere on your own and come back knowing one person's name.
Bring somebody standing on their own into a conversation.
Teach another child to order their own meal, and stand back.

tracks.name: Standing up in front of people
tracks.line: The circle to the room.

steps.test: Say your name and one thing you like, at the welcome circle.
Answer a question out loud in front of the group.
Read something out loud to a room, from the page.
Read it slowly enough that the back of the room hears every word.
steps.note: Everybody speeds up when they are nervous. Slower feels wrong and sounds right.

steps.test: Stand still while you speak, with your hands doing nothing.
Talk for one minute about something you know, with no notes.
Look at three different people while you talk.
Talk for two minutes with no notes.
Start with a question instead of an introduction.
Leave a silence on purpose, and let it sit.
Tell a story standing up, with your voice reaching the back.
Talk for five minutes with three notes on a card.
Take a question afterwards and answer it honestly.
Say "I do not know" to a question, in front of everybody.
Give a five-minute talk and take questions afterwards.
Speak with something going wrong and carry on anyway.
Speak to a room of thirty people.
Speak to a room of fifty people.
Introduce somebody else to a room, and make them look good.
Run the welcome circle at a day out.

tracks.name: Listening
tracks.line: Not interrupting, to coaching somebody.

steps.test: Listen to a whole story without needing to be the one talking.
Let somebody finish a sentence you already knew the end of.
Say back what somebody told you, in your own words, correctly.
Ask one follow-up question instead of telling your own story.
steps.note: The commonest thing people do instead of listening is wait to say their version.

steps.test: Ask three good follow-up questions and get somebody talking.
Notice when somebody has stopped listening to you, and stop.
Listen to somebody you disagree with, all the way through.
Say back their side well enough that they agree that is what they meant.
Listen to somebody much older for an hour, then tell somebody what you learned.
Sit with somebody who is upset without trying to fix it.
Help two people who are arguing sort it out, without taking a side.
Coach somebody through a problem without solving it for them.

tracks.name: Saying the hard thing
tracks.line: Sorry, no, and the truth, all kindly.

steps.test: Say sorry properly, and say what you will do instead.
Say sorry without adding the word but.
Say no, out loud and kindly, when you mean no.
Say no without inventing an excuse for it.
Ask for something you have been putting off asking for.
Say you do not understand, in front of people who seem to.
Admit you were wrong about something, out loud, to the person.
Disagree with somebody without either of you getting upset.
Disagree with somebody older than you, respectfully.
Say the thing everybody in the room is thinking and nobody is saying.
Tell a friend a hard truth, kindly, and stay friends.
Take a piece of criticism without defending yourself.
Ask somebody what you are getting wrong, and listen to the answer.
Give somebody hard feedback and leave them able to act on it.
Have the conversation you have been avoiding for a week.
Argue a case you personally disagree with, well.
Change your own mind out loud, in the middle of an argument.
Repair something with somebody after a row.
Say something kind to somebody that would be easier not to say.
Speak up for somebody who could not speak up for themselves.

tracks.name: Storytelling
tracks.line: One story to holding a room.

steps.test: Tell what happened today in the order it happened.
Tell it in under a minute, with nothing left out that mattered.
Tell a made-up story with a beginning, a middle and an end.
Tell one where somebody wants something and cannot have it.
steps.note: That is the whole engine of every story ever told. Somebody wants something, something is in the way.

steps.test: Tell a story that makes somebody laugh on purpose.
Tell one that makes somebody go quiet.
Learn a story properly and tell it from memory.
Tell it with a pause in the right place.
Tell one round a fire, from memory, that holds everybody.
Tell a story with different voices for each character.
Tell one to younger children and keep them still.
Tell the same story twice and make the second one better.
Tell a true story from your own family.
Get somebody older to tell you theirs, and write it down.
Tell a story with no ending and let the room finish it.
Tell one for five minutes with nobody interrupting.
Tell one to a room of ten.
Tell one to a room of thirty and hold them the whole way.
Tell a story in the dark, with no props and no book.
Teach a younger one to tell theirs, and sit down while they do.

tracks.name: Being funny
tracks.line: One joke to your own material.

steps.test: Tell a joke well enough that somebody laughs.
Tell it again to somebody else and get the same laugh.
Learn five jokes and land all five.
Tell one that dies, and carry on cheerfully.
steps.note: Everybody who is funny has died in front of people. It is the entry fee, not the failure.

steps.test: Make somebody laugh with something you thought of yourself.
Notice what actually made people laugh today, and write it down.
Say the funny thing you thought of instead of keeping it in.
Make a joke about yourself, not about somebody else.
Get a laugh out of a room of five.
Write down ten things you find funny and find what they share.
Write a joke of your own with a proper ending.
Tell three of your own and land two.
Do a funny voice or an impression somebody recognises.
Do two minutes of your own material to a group.
Handle somebody heckling you without losing the room.
Do a sketch or an improv scene with somebody else.
Make somebody laugh who was having a rotten day.
Do five minutes and keep it going.
Get a laugh without saying anything at all.
Run a comedy night and keep it going.

tracks.name: Teaching
tracks.line: One thing to a whole session.

steps.test: Teach one person one thing you can do.
Watch them do it, and say nothing while they get it wrong.
steps.note: Taking it off them to show them again is the commonest mistake in teaching.

steps.test: Teach it well enough that they can still do it a week later.
Break something hard into steps and write the steps down.
Teach it in that order and see where they got stuck.
Change the order because of where they got stuck.
Teach two people at once.
Teach three people at once.
Answer a question you did not know the answer to, honestly.
Teach somebody who did not want to learn it.
Run a whole session for younger children.
Teach an adult something they could not do before.

tracks.name: Saying it yourself
tracks.line: From four, beside you. Your name, a hello, a please, a thank you, a question, a story.

steps.test: Say your name and how old you are to somebody you have not met, looking at them.
Say hello first to somebody you know, before they say it to you.
Say goodbye and their name when you leave.
Ask for something in a whole sentence with a please in it, instead of pointing.
Say thank you to the person at the shop, loud enough that they hear it.
Answer a grown-up who asks you a question, without hiding behind anybody.
Ask a grown-up a question you really want the answer to, and listen to all of it.
Tell somebody you do not want to, in words, instead of crying.
Say sorry to somebody yourself, in your own words.
Order your own food or drink while somebody stands beside you.
Tell somebody something that happened today, with a beginning, a middle and an end.
Tell it to somebody who was not there, so that they understand it.

categories.name: Making and building
categories.line: Wood, cloth, clay, drawing, knots, electronics, machines, code.

tracks.name: Wood
tracks.line: Sanding to furniture.

steps.test: Sand a piece of wood properly smooth.
Sand it again with a finer paper and feel the difference.
Measure a length twice and mark it once.
steps.note: Every ruined piece of wood was measured once.

steps.test: Saw a cut roughly where you marked it.
Saw a straight cut you would be happy to show somebody.
Saw a cut square, checked with a set square.
Drill a hole where you meant it, right through, without splitting the wood.
Drive a screw in flush, without the head chewing up.
Make something from two pieces joined together.
Glue and clamp a joint that holds when it is dry.
Cut a piece to fit a gap you measured, first go.
Draw a plan first, with the sizes on it.
Build exactly what the plan said.
Cut and fit a proper joint — a halving or a housing.
Sharpen a blade and cut with it before and after.
Finish something with oil or wax so it looks finished.
Build something that has to bear weight, and stand on it.
Fix a mistake instead of starting again.
Build a piece of furniture somebody uses every day.
Teach a younger child to saw safely.

tracks.name: Cloth and thread
tracks.line: Threading a needle to clothes you would wear.

steps.test: Thread a needle on your own.
Tie a knot in the end that will not pull through.
Sew a running stitch along a drawn line.
Sew a line of even stitches, all the same length.
Sew on a button that holds when it is pulled.
Sew a seam joining two pieces of cloth.
Mend a rip in something you would still wear out.
Take up a hem and have it stay up.
Darn a hole in a sock or a jumper.
Sew a straight seam on a machine.
Cut cloth to a paper pattern.
Sew a bag you would actually use.
Put in a zip or a drawstring that works.
Press a seam flat and see how much better it looks.
Make a cushion cover or an apron somebody uses.
Fix somebody else's clothes for them.
Alter something that did not fit until it does.
Make something from a pattern, all the way through.
Make a piece of clothing you would wear out of the house.
Teach somebody to sew a button on, and watch them do it.

tracks.name: Knots and rope
tracks.line: One knot to a rope bridge.

steps.test: Tie a knot that does not come undone when pulled.
Tie a reef knot, and say how it differs from a granny.
Tie a bowline.
Tie a bowline round your own waist.
Tie a clove hitch onto a post.
Tie all three from memory with nobody prompting you.
Tie a figure of eight and a taut-line hitch.
Undo a knot that has been loaded hard, without cutting it.
Lash two poles together so they hold your weight.
Whip or tape the end of a rope so it stops fraying.
Build a structure from poles and lashings that holds a person.
Teach three knots to somebody until they can do them blind.

tracks.name: Clay and carving
tracks.line: A pinch pot to something on a shelf.

steps.test: Make a pinch pot that holds water.
Make one with even walls all the way round.
Roll a coil and build a pot from coils.
Join two pieces of clay so they do not crack apart.
steps.note: Score both faces and wet them. Clay that is only pressed together always comes apart.

steps.test: Make something recognisable out of clay.
Make the same thing twice and make the second one better.
Let something dry slowly without it cracking.
Carve a stick into a useful shape with a knife, safely.
steps.note: Always cut away from yourself, and know where the blade goes if it slips.

steps.test: Whittle a point, a notch and a flat face.
Carve a butter knife you would put on a table.
Carve a spoon you would eat with.
Sand and oil something you carved.
Make a set of three things that match.
Make something with a lid that fits.
Decorate a piece so it looks decided rather than accidental.
Fire or bake something so it lasts.
Repair something you broke, visibly and on purpose.
Make something to a size somebody asked for.
Make something somebody puts on a shelf and keeps.
Teach somebody a pinch pot, hands off, all the way through.

tracks.name: Drawing
tracks.line: Recognisable, then good.

steps.test: Draw something and have somebody name it without being told.
Draw the same thing three times and pick the best one.
Draw for ten minutes a day for five days.
Draw something in front of you without lifting the pencil off the paper.
steps.note: It will look strange. It is about looking, not about the drawing.

steps.test: Draw an object by starting with the simple shapes underneath it.
Draw a cube, a cylinder and a ball so that they look solid.
Shade a ball so it looks round, with the light coming from one side.
Draw the same object twice, lit from two different sides.
Draw your own hand, from life.
steps.twist: Draw the hand you draw with, using the other one.

steps.test: Draw the chair you are sitting on, with the legs going the right way.
Draw the gap around an object instead of the object.
steps.note: Draw only the shape of the empty space. Your eye stops guessing and starts looking.

steps.test: Fill a whole page with small drawings of one thing.
steps.twist: Half of them with the other hand.

steps.test: Draw for ten minutes a day for two weeks without missing a day.
Copy a drawing you admire, line for line.
Draw a face with the eyes halfway down the head, not near the top.
steps.note: Almost everybody puts the eyes too high. Halfway down is right, and it fixes a face on its own.

steps.test: Draw a face from a photograph.
Draw the same face again and get the eyes level and the right size.
Draw somebody sitting in front of you, in ten minutes.
Draw somebody you know, and have a third person say who it is.
Draw something somebody asks to keep.

tracks.name: Electricity
tracks.line: One bulb to your own circuit board.

steps.test: Light one bulb with a battery and two wires.
Draw the circuit you just made, as a diagram.
Build a circuit with a switch that works.
Make one where the bulb is dimmer, and say why.
Build one where two things happen at once and explain why.
Wire two bulbs in series, then in parallel, and say what changed.
Use a meter to measure volts across something.
Find a break in a circuit with the meter instead of guessing.
Say what a resistor is for and pick the right one for an LED.
Solder a joint that holds and conducts.
Solder five in a row that all work.
Build a circuit on stripboard from a diagram.
Make a light come on when it gets dark.
Get a microcontroller to blink one light.
Get it to read a button and do something different.
Get it to read a sensor and act on what it reads.
Put it in a box with the wires tidy inside.
Build something that does a job somebody actually wanted.
Fix it when it breaks, without starting again.
Build something other people use, and keep it working.

tracks.name: Machines and code
tracks.line: An idea out loud to something strangers use.

steps.test: Describe an idea for an app out loud, in three clear sentences.
Write down what it should do, in five lines, on paper.
Draw the screens on paper before writing a single word of code.
Make a web page that says your name, and open it in a browser.
Add a button that changes the words when you press it.
Change the colours and the type until it looks like something you would show somebody.
Make a page that adds two numbers you type in.
Break it on purpose, read the error message, and fix it.
steps.note: Reading errors is the whole job. The message almost always says exactly what is wrong.

steps.test: Make it remember what you typed after you close the page.
Ask an AI for a piece you do not understand, then change it to do something else.
Make a list you can add to and delete from.
Put it on the internet with a real address.
Send the address to one person and watch them use it without helping.
Fix the first thing they got stuck on.
Make it work on a phone as well as on a computer.
Add one thing they asked for.
Write down in one sentence what it does, so a stranger would understand.
Let a second person use it with you out of the room.
Change something and put the new version up without breaking the old one.
Have one person use it more than once, because they wanted to.

tracks.name: Photography
tracks.line: A photo to an exhibition.

steps.test: Take a photo where you can tell what it is of.
Take one where the thing you meant is actually in focus.
Get closer, and take it again.
steps.note: Nearly every bad photograph is a photograph taken from too far away.

steps.test: Take one with the light coming from behind you, not behind the subject.
Take one where nothing is growing out of anybody's head.
Take a photo of a person that looks like them.
Take one somebody asks for a copy of.
Take twenty of one thing and pick the best three, and say why.
Take one at the hour before sunset and see the difference.
Put the subject somewhere other than dead centre, on purpose.
Take a photo indoors that is not dark and blurry.
Take one of something moving, sharp.
Take one of the same place in two different lights.
Edit one lightly and keep the original.
Take a set of five that clearly belong together.
Print one and hold it in your hand.
Print and frame one.
Give a printed photograph to the person in it.
Photograph an occasion so that the family keeps the pictures.
Put on a small exhibition of your own photographs.

tracks.name: Scissors
tracks.line: From four, beside you. Cutting, and cutting where you meant to.

steps.test: Open and shut the scissors ten times with nothing in them.
Hold them the right way round, thumb on top, and show somebody.
Cut a piece of paper in two, any way you like.
Snip all along the edge of a piece of paper to make a fringe.
Cut along a straight line somebody drew for you.
Cut a square out.
Cut along a curvy line, all the way, without leaving it.
Cut out a circle and hold it up.
Cut out a shape and turn the paper instead of the scissors.
Fold paper, cut, and open it out to see what happened.
Cut out three shapes and stick them down to make a picture.
Tell somebody what your picture is, while they look at it.

tracks.name: Crayons
tracks.line: From four, beside you. Colouring in, then drawing what you see.

steps.test: Colour one shape in and stay inside the line.
Colour it all the way in, with no white bits left.
Colour a whole picture, every part of it, with more than one colour.
Press hard for a dark colour and softly for a pale one.
Draw a circle that joins up where it started.
Draw a square and a triangle.
Draw a person with a head, a body, two arms and two legs.
Give the person a face, and say who it is.
Draw your house.
Draw somebody standing outside your house.
Draw something that happened today.
Tell the story of your picture to somebody while they look at it.

categories.name: Music and voice
categories.line: Singing, an instrument, rhythm, songs, whistling, reading music.

tracks.name: Singing
tracks.line: A voice warm-up to singing in front of people.

steps.test: Sing one whole song out loud where somebody can hear you.
Do a voice warm-up in the morning, three days running.
Hum a note somebody plays or sings, and match it.
Match five notes in a row.
Do a voice warm-up every morning for one week.
Sing a whole song in tune, on your own, to one person.
Sing standing up, breathing from low down instead of your shoulders.
Sing the same song louder without it going shouty.
Learn a second song properly, words and all.
Do a voice warm-up every morning for thirty days.
Sing a song to a group.
Sing one round with somebody else.
Hold your own line while somebody sings a different one.
Sing a harmony line with somebody else.
